scope: The npm distribution surface: what the published @spec-engine/spec-engine artifact contains and the CLI surfaces that exist only because of it (spec docs, the non-Bun runtime guard). Belongs here: tarball-content promises; the bin wrapper's runtime guard; the offline docs command. Does not belong here: the webapp routes the artifact embeds (SERV); the compiled-binary channel (CI-owned); the docs site content (packages/site). Boundary case: spec docs binds loopback like spec serve, but it is a distribution surface over static files, so the promise lives here.

requirements.statement: The spec docs command serves the prebuilt documentation site over HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1 only, and its --probe mode boots an ephemeral port, fetches /, and exits 0 only when the site title renders.
requirements.why: Docs that need the network die exactly when they are most needed (offline machines, sandboxed agents); a non-loopback bind would expose a local-only tool surface to the network.

requirements.statement: The spec docs command resolves its docs root relative to the running module (import.meta.url) — the npm payload dist/docs/ first, then the checkout build packages/site/dist — and a missing root exits 2 with guidance naming bun run build:site; the lookup is never cwd-relative.
requirements.why: A cwd-relative asset lookup breaks the moment the CLI runs from any directory but the package root — the classic embedded-UI bug; without guidance, a missing docs build reads as a broken install.

requirements.statement: The published bin entry checks for the Bun global before importing the engine bundle and, under any non-Bun runtime, exits 1 with an actionable install hint instead of a module-resolution crash.
requirements.why: The bundle statically imports bun:sqlite, which a Node ESM loader fails to resolve before any inline guard could run; engines.bun is advisory-only and postinstall checks are blocked by Bun's default trust policy, so the wrapper is the only enforcement point.

requirements.statement: The @spec-engine/spec-engine npm artifact ships only the built dist payload (bundle, bin wrapper, docs) plus manifest, README, and LICENSE, and its published dependencies never carry the workspace: protocol.
requirements.why: A tarball with raw source and tests bloats installs and leaks internals, and a single workspace:* string in published dependencies makes the package uninstallable for every consumer.

requirements.statement: The spec docs command shall serve the prebuilt documentation site over HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1 only, with no flag to widen the bind address.
requirements.why: Docs that need the network die exactly when they are most needed (offline machines, sandboxed agents), and a non-loopback bind would expose a local-only tool surface to the network.

requirements.statement: When run with --probe, spec docs shall boot on an ephemeral loopback port, fetch /, and exit 0 only when the site title renders (exit 1 otherwise).
requirements.why: Without a mechanical boot check, a broken docs payload ships silently and is discovered by the first offline user.

requirements.statement: The spec docs command shall locate its docs root relative to the installed module — the npm payload's dist/docs/ first, then a checkout's packages/site/dist — serving the same site from any working directory.
requirements.why: A cwd-relative asset lookup breaks the moment the CLI runs from any directory but the package root — the classic embedded-UI bug.

requirements.statement: If no docs root exists, then spec docs shall exit 2 with guidance naming bun run build:site.
requirements.why: Without guidance, a missing docs build reads as a broken install.

requirements.statement: When run under any non-Bun runtime, the published bin entry shall exit 1 with an actionable hint to install Bun, checking the runtime before importing the engine bundle so no module-resolution crash can precede the message.
requirements.why: The bundle statically imports bun:sqlite, which a Node module loader fails to resolve before any inline guard could run; the wrapper is the only enforcement point.

requirements.statement: The published @spec-engine/spec-engine tarball shall contain only the built dist payload (bundle, bin wrapper, offline docs) plus the package manifest, README, and LICENSE.
requirements.why: A tarball carrying raw source and tests bloats every install and leaks repo internals into the registry.
requirements.deprecatedReason: Tarball file list is packaging layout guarded by the npm-package test, not behavior.

requirements.statement: The published package manifest's dependencies shall never carry the workspace: protocol.
requirements.why: A single workspace:* string in published dependencies makes the package uninstallable for every consumer.

requirements.statement: The README shall name spec init and the NO_SPEC_CONFIG diagnostic, so an adopter reading the warning can find the command that clears it.
requirements.why: An adopter who sees NO_SPEC_CONFIG with no documented command leaves the sibling repo unwired.
requirements.deprecatedReason: A docs-sync check on the README; not product behavior.

requirements.statement: The README and AGENTS.md shall each name SPEC.json, spec migrate, trusted-red, and --results, so the shipped documentation describes the JSON model, the cutover command, and the proof gate.
requirements.why: Documentation that omits the model, the cutover, or the proof gate leaves an adopter on the retired Markdown format or without the trusted-red check.

requirements.statement: The repository shall ship no spec-engine.config.example.json, so spec init stays the only path that authors a member config.
requirements.why: A stale example config gets copied by hand and carries fields spec init no longer writes.
requirements.deprecatedReason: Absence of a repo file; spec init as the only authoring path is covered by INIT-015.

requirements.statement: When a commit lands on main, the release-please job shall open or update one release pull request that bumps the packages/engine version, the release manifest, and packages/engine/CHANGELOG.md from the conventional commits since the last release.
requirements.why: Without it a release depends on a hand bump and a hand tag: a missed bump publishes under a stale version and the changelog is never written.
requirements.deprecatedReason: Release CI process for this repo (release-please job); not product behavior.

requirements.statement: When the release pull request merges or a v* tag is pushed, the CI publish job shall publish @spec-engine/spec-engine to npm through keyless OIDC, in the same workflow run, only after every gate job in that run passes.
requirements.why: A tag release-please creates with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no other workflow, so a publish left to a tag-push run never fires; a publish that skips a gate ships an unvalidated artifact.

requirements.statement: If the release tag does not match the packages/engine package version, then the CI publish job shall fail before packing.
requirements.why: npm versions are immutable: a mismatched publish burns the version number and ships the content under the wrong release.

requirements.statement: The repository shall declare every dependency as an exact version and carry a Renovate config that keeps those pins exact and current.
requirements.why: A range resolves to whatever the registry serves on install day, so two installs of one commit diverge; exact pins nobody updates rot into unpatched versions.
requirements.deprecatedReason: Dependency-pinning and Renovate hygiene for this repo; not product behavior.

requirements.statement: The README and the agent reference shall each name SPEC.json, spec migrate, trusted-red, and --results, so the shipped documentation describes the JSON model, the cutover command, and the proof gate.
requirements.why: Documentation that omits the model, the cutover, or the proof gate leaves an adopter on the retired Markdown format or without the trusted-red check.
requirements.deprecatedReason: A docs-sync check on README and the agent reference; not product behavior.

requirements.statement: The published npm package shall carry the agent reference, the req-author skill, an MCP server template, and a pre-commit hook template in an agent folder of its payload.
requirements.why: An adopter installing from npm gets only the CLI otherwise, and spec init has no bundled reference, skill, or templates to install into the repository.

requirements.statement: The spec docs command shall serve the same documentation site from any working directory.
requirements.why: A cwd-relative asset lookup breaks the moment the CLI runs from any directory but the package root — the classic embedded-UI bug.

requirements.statement: When the published spec command runs under a runtime other than Bun, it shall exit 1 with a hint to install Bun.
requirements.why: The bundle statically imports bun:sqlite, which a Node module loader fails to resolve before any inline guard could run; the wrapper is the only enforcement point.

requirements.statement: The published spec package shall install from the npm registry without a repository checkout.
requirements.why: A single workspace:* string in published dependencies makes the package uninstallable for every consumer.

requirements.statement: When a release is cut, the engine shall publish to npm only after every CI gate has passed.
requirements.why: A tag release-please creates with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no other workflow, so a publish left to a tag-push run never fires; a publish that skips a gate ships an unvalidated artifact.
